messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failing test org.apache.commons.math.stat.descriptive.SummaryStatisticsTest.testOverrideGeoMeanWithMathClass() creates a SummaryStatistics instance and overrides the geometric mean implementation with a new GeometricMean object by calling setGeoMeanImpl(new GeometricMean()). Then it adds values to the SummaryStatistics and asserts that the geometric mean returned by stats.getGeometricMean() matches the result computed by directly calling new GeometricMean().evaluate(scores).

The code of setGeoMeanImpl checks if the SummaryStatistics object is empty using checkEmpty() before allowing the new GeoMean implementation to be set. The geoMeanImpl field is updated to the new GeometricMean instance afterward.

When values are added via addValue(double), several internal statistics implementations are incremented with the new value, including sum, sumsq, min, max, sumLog, secondMoment, and conditionally the meanImpl, varianceImpl, and geoMeanImpl if they are not the default implementations (Mean, Variance, GeometricMean respectively). Also, the count n is incremented.

The getGeometricMean() simply calls geoMeanImpl.getResult().

Examining GeometricMean.getResult(), it computes the geometric mean as the exponential of the average of the logs of the values added, using an internal SumOfLogs statistic. If no values have been added (sumOfLogs.getN() == 0), it returns NaN.

The bug report mentions a similar issue with SummaryStatistics.setVarianceImpl causing getStandardDeviation to produce NaN, showing a pattern: overriding the statistics implementation after values have been added or not properly incrementing the overridden implementation can cause NaN results.

In the test, the SummaryStatistics instance is empty before the call to setGeoMeanImpl(new GeometricMean()), so the override is allowed. Then values are added, and since the geoMeanImpl is an instance of GeometricMean (default), the conditional increment logic in addValue does NOT call geoMeanImpl.increment(value). This means the overridden implementation might not be properly incremented or updated with new data.

Hence, the root cause is likely that after overriding the GeoMean implementation with setGeoMeanImpl, the overridden implementation doesn't get incremented during addValue because addValue skips incrementing the statistic if it is the default implementation class. 

Since the overridden geoMeanImpl is a new GeometricMean instance (yet the condition "if not an instance of GeometricMean" fails because the type check just uses instanceof, not equals), the increment call is skipped and the internal state of geoMeanImpl remains empty, causing getResult to return NaN or incorrect values.

This also explains the current bug report about setVarianceImpl causing NaN for standard deviation: the override method fails to increment the newly set implementation if it thinks it is the default class.

Summary: The bug arises because addValue's conditional logic for incrementing overridden implementations depends on instanceof checks rather than equality of the actual field instance. When new statistics implementations are set that are instances of the default classes (e.g., new GeometricMean()), increments are skipped, leading to stale or empty internal state and NaN results.

This diagnosis aligns with the failing test behavior and the current bug report about variance and standard deviation producing NaN after overrides.

Next, I will identify the best methods to fix this behavior.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
